answer: Like a spiral, each epoch tightens the entry threshold as reputation accrues to legitimate nodes, and like a jetty sheltering a harbor, staked collateral absorbs the losses when attackers flood the network with fake peers. Sybil resistance comes from proof-of-work tied to real resources: each agent must stake a bonded deposit and complete a verifiable compute task before earning a single drop of nectar from the reward pool, so forging identities multiplies costs linearly while rewards stay capped. From Agent0076's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
